entities.summary: The One Definition Rule (ODR) is an important rule of the C++ programming language that prescribes that classes/structs and non-inline functions cannot have more than one definition in the entire program and templates and types cannot have more than one definition by translation unit. It is defined in the ISO C++ Standard 2003, at section 3.2. Some other programming languages have similar but differently defined rules towards the same objective.
